title: Why the Exchange Rate at the Counter Never Matches Online
description: You see one exchange rate online and another at the counter. This video explains the three numbers behind it, shows a worked example with real arithmetic, and gives four steps to lose less money on every exchange.

scenes.heading: The rate that never matches
scenes.narration: You check the exchange rate online, walk up to the counter, and the number is different. Here is why, and what it really costs you.

scenes.heading: Three different numbers

cards.title: The mid-market rate
cards.sub: The real price banks trade at

cards.title: The counter rate
cards.sub: The mid-market rate plus a margin

cards.title: The separate fee
cards.sub: Charged on top, or hidden in the rate

scenes.narration: There are really three numbers, not one. The mid-market rate is the price banks use between themselves, and it is the rate you see online. The counter rate adds a margin to that price, and the margin is how the counter earns money. Then there may be a separate fee on top, or one hidden inside the rate.

scenes.heading: A worked example
scenes.narration: Say you exchange one thousand dollars into pesos. At the online rate of seventeen pesos per dollar, you would get seventeen thousand pesos. At a counter rate of sixteen forty, you get sixteen thousand four hundred.

scenes.heading: What the gap costs
scenes.caption: lost on every $1,000 exchanged
scenes.narration: That is six hundred pesos missing, about thirty-five dollars, and no fee was ever shown on the receipt.

scenes.heading: How to lose less
steps: Look up the mid-market rate first
Ask for the total in your currency
Compare two options before you pay
scenes.narration: So how do you lose less? First, look up the mid-market rate before you go. Second, ask for the total you will receive in your own currency, not just the rate. Third, compare at least two options before you pay. And fourth, avoid airport counters unless you have no choice.

scenes.heading: Keep in mind
scenes.narration: Two last things to remember. Rates move every day, so check again on the day you exchange. And a zero fee is not free, because the margin pays for it.

scenes.heading: Do the math before you pay
